question: On a pull request's head: after a push, is every required check pending again; does a required check conclude `timed_out`, `neutral`, `skipped`, `cancelled` or `stale` and keep that conclusion until the content changes or a person runs it again; is every check run read with its exact name and its App's id, two workflow runs on one commit both staying, since `filter=latest` is per check suite; and can any App with `checks: write`, or any Actions job, post a check run under a required Lens's check name, or a result for any criterion of a contract, one the contract does not name among them, which then stays on that head?
pass: Written 2026-11-03T03:32:48Z, before the run (issue 250, its rules a_check_reports_on_its_own, a_check_is_read_by_name_from_every_app and a_rerun_replaces_only_its_own_run, which P-42 left waiting since it never read the status rollup the port reads): on a new canary pull request from branch trial/p-42r to main that changes only p42/r.md, so that p2-queue runs on pull_request and p42-checks on pull_request and on push, two suites on one commit, with every write the Maintainer's and not recorded here. (1) The head's statusCheckRollup, read at once, holds the required check p2-queue-check not yet concluded, and a read some minutes later holds it concluded, success or failure, with nothing done between but reads. (2) Every check run REST lists on the head with filter=latest is in the rollup once, by its exact name, with the id of its check suite's App, the two suites of p42-checks both there; the head of canary pull request 65, where the pr-review App and an Actions job each posted (trials/P-42.json), is read the same way, for a second App. (3) After the Maintainer re-runs one job of one run, the rollup holds that job's new run in its suite and not the old one, filter=all lists both, and the other suite's run of the same name stays. Pass if (1), (2) and (3) hold; fail otherwise, each part recorded. Run on 2026-11-03 on canary pull request 92, opened, closed and its branch deleted by the Maintainer's login (writes not recorded here). Passed. (1) The first read with the required check in it held p2-queue-check QUEUED; 64 reads later, 11 minutes on, with nothing done between but reads, it read COMPLETED, SUCCESS. (2) With every run concluded, the rollup held the same 17 check runs, by id, name, suite and App, as filter=latest: four Apps (GitHub Actions 15368, CodeRabbit 347564, github-advanced-security 57789, whose runs are CodeQL's and SonarCloud's uploads, and sonarqubecloud 12526), the two suites of p42-checks both there. Pull request 65's head read the same, 15 and 15, three Apps; the pr-review App's posts of P-42 are on that pull request's earlier head, so none of them is here. (3) The Maintainer's re-run of p42 / timed-out in the pull_request suite (gh run rerun --job) made that run's attempt 2: it ran that job again, and gave each of the run's other jobs a new check run in the same suite with the old one's times, though they did not run again. The rollup then held the four new check runs and not the old ones, filter=latest again the same 17, filter=all both of each, and the push suite's p42 / timed-out stayed as it was. The rollup also drops a post. Each run of p42 / posts created p2-queue-check, p42 / neutral and an unlisted criterion's run, all six in the push suite, the first Actions suite of that commit (decision 0103). filter=all lists both of each, and the rollup and filter=latest hold the later one alone. So the rollup reads the latest run of each name in each check suite, from every App, whether the run before it was re-run or posted again. A post in the required check's own suite would stand in its place. Here every post landed in another suite, so p2-queue-check read twice, once from p2-queue's suite and once from p42-checks'.

-   Fast, precise static analysis and feedback on your code

app.description:
SonarQube Cloud (formerly SonarCloud) is a SaaS code analysis tool designed to detect coding issues in 30+ languages, frameworks, and IaC platforms. Your code is checked against an extensive set of rules that cover many attributes of code, such as maintainability, reliability, and security issues, on each merge/pull request.

For those requiring US-based hosting, [SonarQube Cloud US](https://sonarqube.us/) offers the perfect alternative. If you need data residency outside the US or within the EU, [SonarQube Cloud](https://sonarcloud.io/) with this GitHub app is the ideal solution.

SonarQube Cloud integrates seamlessly into your GitHub workflow and provides clear guidance for resolving any code quality and security issues detected. The majority of popular languages can be analyzed automatically; no configuration is required!

With [SonarQube Cloud](https://sonarcloud.io/github), you get:

-   Fast, precise static analysis and feedback on your code
    
-   Support for popular languages, frameworks, and IaC tools
    
-   Free analysis for open-source projects and private projects up to max 50k LoC
    
-   Automatic analysis of pull requests and branches with results reported inline
    
-   IDE Support with [SonarQube for IDE](https://www.sonarsource.com/products/sonarlint/) integration
    
-   Quality Gate (added as a GitHub check) acting at two different levels - first, preventing you from merging pull requests that contain issues - and later, helping you to release only clean, safe code
    
-   Sign up for SonarQube free tier and begin scanning your private and public repositories
    

A [GitHub Action](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/sonarcloud-scan) is available in the marketplace to make it easy for you (for projects where automatic analysis isn't available). SonarQube Cloud also integrates smoothly with Jenkins, CircleCI, TravisCI, CirrusCI, and many other tools.

A free tier is available that allows you to explore the benefits of SonarQube Cloud using your public and private repositories. We also provide a no-commitment, [14-day trial](https://www.sonarsource.com/products/sonarcloud/signup/) of SonarQube Cloud Team for unlimited team members, up to 1.9M LoC, AI CodeFix recommendations, and more. No need to speak with a sales rep or request a license key - get automatic code analysis results on your private projects in minutes! Want to see more examples of SonarCloud in action? You can [explore current Open Source projects in SonarCloud](https://sonarcloud.io/explore/projects?sort=-analysis_date) that are using the [Clean as You Code](https://www.sonarsource.com/solutions/our-unique-approach/) methodology.

What are you waiting for? SonarQube Cloud helps you consistently deliver cleaner, secure software that future developers will appreciate and your users will love. Start writing Clean Code. [Now](https://www.sonarsource.com/products/sonarcloud/signup/)!
